source.citation: W. E. S. Trowbridge. Drawing of the Sauganash Hotel, Mark Beaubien's tavern on Lake Street near Market Street — signed "W. E. S. Trowbridge" at the lower left. Reproduced on Chicagology, "Lake Street", captioned "A drawing by W. E. S. Trowbridge of Mark Beaubien's Sauganash hotel on Lake st. near Market st. It was built in 1831. It burned down in 1851."
what_it_does_not_supply: any coordinate, footprint outline or dimension
its own date — the plate as reproduced does not give a legible year
independent corroboration of the Braunhold engraving: it belongs to the same retrospective descent
the state of the building on 1 July 1835 as against any other year of its 1831-1851 life
what_it_supplies: louvred shutters flanking the sash of the clapboard block
a tall vertical-board fence enclosing the ground behind and to the right of the building
hitching or corner posts standing at the road edge in front of the frontage
the log wing attached at the left, single-storey, under its own shingled roof, its door opening direct to grade
the clapboard block's two brick chimneys and its entrance without a veranda or gallery
